canonicalExplanation.summary: **Generics** let one class or method work with many types while the compiler still tracks **which** type. `class Box<T>` has a **type parameter** T; `Box<String>` stores and returns Strings, with no casts. A **generic method** declares its own parameter before the return type: `static <T> T first(List<T> items)` returns whatever element type the list holds. The payoff is **compile-time safety**: putting an Integer in a `Box<String>` is an error before the program runs. The catch is **erasure**: at run time the type argument is gone, so you **can't** write `new T()`, `new T[10]` or `x instanceof T`. Avoid **raw types** like plain `Box`, which switch the checks off.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner stores everything in `List` (raw) and casts on the way out: `String s = (String) list.get(0);`. One day an Integer sneaks in and the cast throws ClassCastException far from where the bad value was added. Then they try `new T()` inside a generic class and the compiler refuses. Box<T> stores and returns T, while a static <T> T first(List<T>) method preserves the list element type at each call. In this lesson you'll implement and use a small generic class and generic method safely.

Erasure limits

Use type inference and explain erasure limits such as new T().

outcomes: Implement and use a small generic class and generic method safely.

examples.title: A Box<T> and a first(List<T>) method
examples.situation: Box<T> stores and returns T, while a static <T> T first(List<T>) method preserves the list element type at each call.
walkthrough: **Box<T> stores and returns T:** Box<String>.get() returns a String with no cast.
**A static <T> T first(List<T>) method:** the method declares T before its return type.
**Preserves the list element type at each call:** first(List.of(7, 8, 9)) will return an Integer, and first on a List<String> returns a String.
examples.result: One implementation serves every element type, checked at compile time.

examples.title: The cast that exploded later
examples.situation: A raw List collects strings and one Integer, and a cast to String throws when the list is read.
walkthrough: The raw type let the Integer in with only a warning.
Now the compiler rejects the bad add at the line that caused it.
examples.result: The bug is caught at compile time, where it was written.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Generic type arguments are fully reified at runtime, so new T() and new T[10] are always available.
misconceptions.correction: Type arguments are erased after compilation. Code can't create T values or T arrays directly; pass a factory or use a List<T> instead.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, why couldn't Box create a new T?

analogy.example: A generic class is like **a labelled storage bin**: `Box<String>` has a "strings only" label the **checker at the door** (the compiler) enforces. But the label is **peeled off before shipping** (erasure), so the warehouse at run time can't read it to build new items of that kind.
usefulFor: remembering labels checked at the door
limitations: A raw type is a bin with no label: anything goes in.
Inference is the checker reading the label for you.

steps.explanation: The diamond infers T as String from the constructor argument.
Box<T> stores and returns T, so no cast is needed.
A static <T> T first(List<T>) method preserves the list element type at each call.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing generic type inference. Step 1, Create: Box type is Box<String>; value is "Ada". The diamond infers T as String from the constructor argument. Step 2, Get: returned type is String; cast is none. Box<T> stores and returns T, so no cast is needed. Step 3, Call generic: T is Integer; result is 7. nearTransfer.prompt: Write a generic class Pair<A, B> with accessors and a generic method static <T> T last(List<T>). Test with Pair<String, Integer> and lists of two types.
expectedEvidence: A wrong type fails to compile.

farTransfer.prompt: Build a generic Cache<K, V> backed by a HashMap with get, put and a getOrCreate(K key, Supplier<V> maker) method. Explain why a Supplier is needed instead of new V().
scaffold: Call maker.get() only on a miss.
expectedEvidence: Works for two different V types.

remediation.explanation: When you see a cast on the way out of a container, ask: **could a type parameter carry this type instead?** Replace raw types with parameterised ones.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The cast that exploded later".

recap.summary: To implement and use a small generic class and generic method safely, declare type parameters, let the compiler infer type arguments, avoid raw types and casts, and remember erasure means no new T() or new T[] at run time.
